Who is it that hit you?”"}]},{"verse":69,"paragraph_start":true,"segments":[{"speaker":"narrator","text":"Now Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard, and a slave girl came up to him and said,"},{"speaker":"other","text":"“You too were with Jesus the Galilean.”"}]},{"verse":70,"paragraph_start":false,"segments":[{"speaker":"narrator","text":"But he denied it in front of them all, saying,"},{"speaker":"other","text":"“I do not know what you are talking about.”"}]},{"verse":71,"paragraph_start":false,"segments":[{"speaker":"narrator","text":"When he had gone out to the gateway, another woman saw him and said to those who were there,"},{"speaker":"other","text":"“This man was with Jesus the Nazarene.”"}]},{"verse":72,"paragraph_start":false,"segments":[{"speaker":"narrator","text":"And again he denied it, with an oath:"},{"speaker":"other","text":"“I do not know the man.”"}]},{"verse":73,"paragraph_start":false,"segments":[{"speaker":"narrator","text":"After a little while the bystanders came up and said to Peter,"},{"speaker":"other","text":"“Surely you too are one of them, for the way you speak gives you away.”"}]},{"verse":74,"paragraph_start":false,"segments":[{"speaker":"narrator","text":"Then he began to call down curses and to swear,"},{"speaker":"other","text":"“I do not know the man!”"},{"speaker":"narrator","text":"And immediately a rooster crowed."}]},{"verse":75,"paragraph_start":false,"segments":[{"speaker":"narrator","text":"And Peter remembered the word Jesus had spoken:"},{"speaker":"Jesus","text":"“Before a rooster crows, you will deny me three times.”"},{"speaker":"narrator","text":"And he went outside and wept bitterly."}]}],"notes":[{"verse":2,"phrase":"handed over","lemma":"παραδίδωμι","kind":"departure","traditional":"betrayed (of Judas); delivered up","note":"The Greek verb means to hand someone over into another's custody or power; Greek has a different word for 'betray'. Matthew uses this one verb for what Judas does, for what happens to the Son of Man, and later for what the authorities do to Jesus, and a single rendering keeps those links visible. Most translations use 'betray' where Judas is the subject and 'deliver' or 'hand over' elsewhere."},{"verse":13,"phrase":"good news","lemma":"εὐαγγέλιον","kind":"departure","traditional":"gospel","note":"The Greek word meant a welcome announcement, such as news of a victory, and a first-century hearer heard that ordinary sense. 'Gospel' once meant the same but now suggests a book or a body of doctrine. Many translations keep 'gospel' here; several modern ones use 'good news'."},{"verse":15,"phrase":"weighed out thirty silver coins","lemma":"ἵστημι","kind":"background","traditional":"covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver","note":"The verb is literally 'set' or 'weighed', the old way of paying in silver, and the wording echoes the Greek version of Zechariah 11:12, where a shepherd's wages are weighed out as thirty pieces of silver. Thirty shekels of silver is also the compensation set in Exodus 21:32 for a slave killed by an ox. Some translations render 'counted out' or 'agreed to pay'."},{"verse":25,"phrase":"You have said it","lemma":"","kind":"ambiguity","traditional":"You have said so","note":"The reply is an indirect affirmation: it concedes the point while leaving the words in the questioner's mouth. Some read it as a plain 'Yes', others as more reserved ('That is your way of putting it'). Jesus gives the same answer to the high priest in verse 64, where what follows shows it is not a denial."},{"verse":28,"phrase":"of the covenant","lemma":"διαθήκη","kind":"textual","traditional":"of the new testament; of the new covenant","note":"Many later manuscripts read 'the new covenant', the wording behind the King James Version. The earliest witnesses lack 'new', which was probably added from the parallel wording in Luke 22:20 and 1 Corinthians 11:25. The phrase 'blood of the covenant' recalls Exodus 24:8."},{"verse":41,"phrase":"testing","lemma":"πειρασμός","kind":"departure","traditional":"temptation","note":"The Greek noun covers both a trial that tests a person and an enticement to do wrong. Here the coming arrest is a test of the disciples' loyalty rather than a lure to sin, so 'testing' is used. 'Temptation' is the traditional rendering, and some modern translations have 'the time of trial'."},{"verse":45,"phrase":"Are you still sleeping and resting?","lemma":"","kind":"ambiguity","traditional":"Sleep on now, and take your rest","note":"The Greek can be read as a question, as a command (perhaps ironic), or as an exclamation. The traditional rendering is the command, but it sits awkwardly with 'Get up, let us go' in the next verse, and many modern translations read a question, as here. The phrase rendered 'still' could also mean 'from now on' or 'for the time that remains'."},{"verse":50,"phrase":"do what you are here for","lemma":"","kind":"ambiguity","traditional":"wherefore art thou come?","note":"The Greek is a terse fragment, literally 'for what you are here'. It can be completed as a command, as here and in most modern translations, or as a question ('Why have you come?'), as in older versions. The word rendered 'Friend' is not the usual word for a friend but an address to a companion or associate; in Matthew's two other uses (20:13; 22:12) it addresses someone in the wrong."},{"verse":51,"phrase":"slave","lemma":"δοῦλος","kind":"departure","traditional":"servant","note":"The Greek word denotes a slave, a person owned by a master, not a hired servant. English Bibles have traditionally softened it to 'servant'; several recent translations use 'slave' or 'bondservant'. The 'slave girl' of verse 69 is likewise a female household slave in Greek."},{"verse":55,"phrase":"bandit","lemma":"λῃστής","kind":"departure","traditional":"thief; robber","note":"The Greek word means an armed robber or brigand, someone who uses violence, not a sneak thief; Josephus also uses it of armed insurgents. Older translations have 'thief' or 'robber', and some modern ones have 'bandit' or 'one leading a rebellion'. The same word describes the two men crucified with Jesus in the next chapter."},{"verse":63,"phrase":"the Messiah","lemma":"Χριστός","kind":"departure","traditional":"the Christ","note":"The Greek word is the one usually rendered 'Christ'. Here it is a title, the anointed king Israel expected, and the high priest is asking whether Jesus claims that office; 'Messiah' conveys the title where 'Christ' now reads as a name. Several modern translations make the same choice in the Gospels."},{"verse":64,"phrase":"the Power","lemma":"δύναμις","kind":"background","traditional":"power","note":"'The Power' is a reverent Jewish way of referring to God without naming him. The sentence combines Psalm 110:1 (seated at God's right hand) with Daniel 7:13 (one like a son of man coming with the clouds of heaven), and it is this claim that the high priest treats as blasphemy."},{"verse":74,"phrase":"call down curses","lemma":"καταθεματίζω","kind":"ambiguity","traditional":"began to curse","note":"The Greek verb has no object. Most take it that Peter called down curses on himself if he was lying, to strengthen his oath; a minority view is that he cursed Jesus to prove he was no disciple. The rendering leaves the object unstated, as the Greek does."}],"candidates":[{"lemma":"παραδίδωμι","rendering":"hand over","verse":2,"reason":"Translations split between 'betray', 'deliver' and 'hand over' depending on the subject, which hides a thread running through the passion narratives and the letters."},{"lemma":"εὐαγγέλιον","rendering":"good news","verse":13,"reason":"It recurs across the whole New Testament and the choice between 'gospel' and 'good news' should be made once."},{"lemma":"δοῦλος","rendering":"slave","verse":51,"reason":"It is very frequent, and whether it is rendered 'slave' or 'servant' affects narrative, parables and Paul's self-descriptions alike."},{"lemma":"πειρασμός","rendering":"testing","verse":41,"reason":"The choice between 'temptation', 'testing' and 'trial' recurs in the Lord's Prayer, the Gospels, James and 1 Peter, and readers will notice if it varies."},{"lemma":"σκανδαλίζω","rendering":"fall away","verse":31,"reason":"Translations vary widely ('offend', 'stumble', 'fall away', 'cause to sin') for a word frequent in the Gospels and Paul."}]}

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When Jesus had finished all these words, he said to his disciples,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You know that after two days the Passover comes, and the Son of Man is handed over to be crucified.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then the chief priests and the elders of the people gathered in the courtyard of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and they plotted together to seize Jesus by deceit and kill him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But they were saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Not during the festival, or there may be a riot among the people.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now when Jesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: a woman came to him with an alabaster jar of very costly perfumed oil, and she poured it over his head as he reclined at table.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When the disciples saw this, they were indignant and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Why this waste?

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: This could have been sold for a high price and given to the poor.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Jesus, aware of this, said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Why are you making trouble for the woman? She has done a good deed for me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For you always have the poor with you, but you do not always have me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: When she poured this perfumed oil on my body, she did it to prepare me for burial.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Truly I tell you, wherever this good news is proclaimed in the whole world, what she has done will also be told, in memory of her.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then one of the Twelve, the one called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “What are you willing to give me if I hand him over to you?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They weighed out thirty silver coins for him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And from then on he was looking for an opportunity to hand him over.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: On the first day of Unleavened Bread the disciples came to Jesus and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Where do you want us to prepare for you to eat the Passover?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Go into the city to a certain man and say to him, ‘The Teacher says: My time is near; I am keeping the Passover at your house with my disciples.’”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The disciples did as Jesus had directed them, and they prepared the Passover.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When evening came, he was reclining at table with the twelve disciples,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and while they were eating he said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Truly I tell you, one of you will hand me over.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They were deeply grieved, and each one began to say to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Surely it is not I, Lord?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He answered,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “The one who has dipped his hand in the bowl with me, he will hand me over.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: The Son of Man goes as it is written about him, but woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is handed over! It would have been better for that man if he had not been born.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Judas, the one who was handing him over, answered,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Surely it is not I, Rabbi?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You have said it.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: While they were eating, Jesus took bread, and after saying the blessing he broke it, gave it to the disciples, and said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Take, eat; this is my body.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he took a cup, and after giving thanks he gave it to them, saying,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Drink from it, all of you,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: for this is my blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I tell you, from now on I will not drink of this fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new with you in my Father’s kingdom.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And after singing a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “All of you will fall away because of me this night, for it is written, ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But after I have been raised, I will go ahead of you to Galilee.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Peter answered him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Even if all fall away because of you, I will never fall away.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Truly I tell you, this very night, before a rooster crows, you will deny me three times.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Peter said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Even if I must die with you, I will never deny you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And all the disciples said the same.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then Jesus came with them to a place called Gethsemane, and he said to the disciples,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Sit here while I go over there and pray.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Taking with him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, he began to be grieved and deeply troubled.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “My soul is overwhelmed with grief, to the point of death. Remain here and stay awake with me.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Going a little farther, he fell on his face, praying and saying,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me. Yet not as I will, but as you will.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he came to the disciples and found them sleeping, and he said to Peter,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “So none of you had the strength to stay awake with me for one hour?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Stay awake and pray, so that you do not enter into testing. The spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Again, a second time, he went away and prayed,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “My Father, if this cannot pass unless I drink it, your will be done.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And when he came back he again found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So he left them, went away again, and prayed a third time, saying the same words once more.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he came to the disciples and said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Are you still sleeping and resting? Look, the hour has come near, and the Son of Man is being handed over into the hands of sinners.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Get up, let us go. Look, the one handing me over has come near.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: While he was still speaking, Judas, one of the Twelve, arrived, and with him a large crowd with swords and clubs, sent from the chief priests and elders of the people.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now the one handing him over had given them a sign, saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “The one I kiss is the man; seize him.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He went straight up to Jesus and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Greetings, Rabbi!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and kissed him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Friend, do what you are here for.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then they came forward, laid hands on Jesus, and seized him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And one of those with Jesus reached out his hand, drew his sword, struck the high priest’s slave, and cut off his ear.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then Jesus said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Put your sword back in its place, for all who take up the sword will perish by the sword.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Or do you think that I cannot call on my Father, and he will at once put at my side more than twelve legions of angels?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: How then would the scriptures be fulfilled, that it must happen this way?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: At that hour Jesus said to the crowds,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Have you come out with swords and clubs to arrest me, as if against a bandit? Day after day I sat in the temple teaching, and you did not seize me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But all this has happened so that the scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then all the disciples left him and fled.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Those who had seized Jesus led him away to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and the elders had gathered.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Peter was following him at a distance, as far as the high priest’s courtyard, and going inside he sat with the attendants to see how it would end.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now the chief priests and the whole council were looking for false testimony against Jesus so that they could put him to death,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: but they found none, though many false witnesses came forward. At last two came forward

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “This man said, ‘I am able to destroy the temple of God and rebuild it in three days.’”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The high priest stood up and said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Do you answer nothing? What is it that these men testify against you?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Jesus kept silent. And the high priest said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “I put you under oath by the living God: tell us whether you are the Messiah, the Son of God.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You have said it. But I tell you, from now on you will see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of the Power and coming on the clouds of heaven.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then the high priest tore his clothes and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “He has blasphemed! What further need do we have of witnesses? Look, now you have heard the blasphemy.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: What do you think?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They answered,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “He deserves death.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then they spat in his face and struck him with their fists, and some slapped him,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Prophesy to us, Messiah! Who is it that hit you?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard, and a slave girl came up to him and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “You too were with Jesus the Galilean.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But he denied it in front of them all, saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “I do not know what you are talking about.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When he had gone out to the gateway, another woman saw him and said to those who were there,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “This man was with Jesus the Nazarene.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And again he denied it, with an oath:

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “I do not know the man.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After a little while the bystanders came up and said to Peter,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Surely you too are one of them, for the way you speak gives you away.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he began to call down curses and to swear,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “I do not know the man!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And immediately a rooster crowed.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And Peter remembered the word Jesus had spoken:

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Before a rooster crows, you will deny me three times.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he went outside and wept bitterly.

notes.note: The Greek verb means to hand someone over into another's custody or power; Greek has a different word for 'betray'. Matthew uses this one verb for what Judas does, for what happens to the Son of Man, and later for what the authorities do to Jesus, and a single rendering keeps those links visible. Most translations use 'betray' where Judas is the subject and 'deliver' or 'hand over' elsewhere.

The Greek word meant a welcome announcement, such as news of a victory, and a first-century hearer heard that ordinary sense. 'Gospel' once meant the same but now suggests a book or a body of doctrine. Many translations keep 'gospel' here; several modern ones use 'good news'.

notes.traditional: covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver
notes.note: The verb is literally 'set' or 'weighed', the old way of paying in silver, and the wording echoes the Greek version of Zechariah 11:12, where a shepherd's wages are weighed out as thirty pieces of silver. Thirty shekels of silver is also the compensation set in Exodus 21:32 for a slave killed by an ox. Some translations render 'counted out' or 'agreed to pay'.

The reply is an indirect affirmation: it concedes the point while leaving the words in the questioner's mouth. Some read it as a plain 'Yes', others as more reserved ('That is your way of putting it'). Jesus gives the same answer to the high priest in verse 64, where what follows shows it is not a denial.

notes.traditional: of the new testament; of the new covenant
notes.note: Many later manuscripts read 'the new covenant', the wording behind the King James Version. The earliest witnesses lack 'new', which was probably added from the parallel wording in Luke 22:20 and 1 Corinthians 11:25. The phrase 'blood of the covenant' recalls Exodus 24:8.

The Greek noun covers both a trial that tests a person and an enticement to do wrong. Here the coming arrest is a test of the disciples' loyalty rather than a lure to sin, so 'testing' is used. 'Temptation' is the traditional rendering, and some modern translations have 'the time of trial'.

notes.phrase: Are you still sleeping and resting?
notes.traditional: Sleep on now, and take your rest
notes.note: The Greek can be read as a question, as a command (perhaps ironic), or as an exclamation. The traditional rendering is the command, but it sits awkwardly with 'Get up, let us go' in the next verse, and many modern translations read a question, as here. The phrase rendered 'still' could also mean 'from now on' or 'for the time that remains'.

notes.phrase: do what you are here for
notes.note: The Greek is a terse fragment, literally 'for what you are here'. It can be completed as a command, as here and in most modern translations, or as a question ('Why have you come?'), as in older versions. The word rendered 'Friend' is not the usual word for a friend but an address to a companion or associate; in Matthew's two other uses (20:13; 22:12) it addresses someone in the wrong.

The Greek word denotes a slave, a person owned by a master, not a hired servant. English Bibles have traditionally softened it to 'servant'; several recent translations use 'slave' or 'bondservant'. The 'slave girl' of verse 69 is likewise a female household slave in Greek.

The Greek word means an armed robber or brigand, someone who uses violence, not a sneak thief; Josephus also uses it of armed insurgents. Older translations have 'thief' or 'robber', and some modern ones have 'bandit' or 'one leading a rebellion'. The same word describes the two men crucified with Jesus in the next chapter.

The Greek word is the one usually rendered 'Christ'. Here it is a title, the anointed king Israel expected, and the high priest is asking whether Jesus claims that office; 'Messiah' conveys the title where 'Christ' now reads as a name. Several modern translations make the same choice in the Gospels.

'The Power' is a reverent Jewish way of referring to God without naming him. The sentence combines Psalm 110:1 (seated at God's right hand) with Daniel 7:13 (one like a son of man coming with the clouds of heaven), and it is this claim that the high priest treats as blasphemy.

The Greek verb has no object. Most take it that Peter called down curses on himself if he was lying, to strengthen his oath; a minority view is that he cursed Jesus to prove he was no disciple. The rendering leaves the object unstated, as the Greek does.

candidates.reason: Translations split between 'betray', 'deliver' and 'hand over' depending on the subject, which hides a thread running through the passion narratives and the letters.
It recurs across the whole New Testament and the choice between 'gospel' and 'good news' should be made once.
It is very frequent, and whether it is rendered 'slave' or 'servant' affects narrative, parables and Paul's self-descriptions alike.
The choice between 'temptation', 'testing' and 'trial' recurs in the Lord's Prayer, the Gospels, James and 1 Peter, and readers will notice if it varies.
Translations vary widely ('offend', 'stumble', 'fall away', 'cause to sin') for a word frequent in the Gospels and Paul.
